features.label: WebRTC tests

features.summary: WebRTC tests that had been disabled or restricted on macOS, Linux, and Windows were updated to match where they now pass, with Android media tests adjusted for isolated processes. Data-channel interoperability tests also get more realistic timing and corrected API spelling, helping keep cross-platform WebRTC behavior dependable.

features.label: Connection transport (ICE / DTLS)

patches.author: Andrew Osmond
patches.subject: Don't create candidate pairs from binding responses on an obsolete ICE stream.

features.summary: These changes tighten ICE connection setup and DTLS, the protocol that encrypts WebRTC connections. Firefox now rejects an empty encryption-cipher list and avoids creating connections from replies tied to an outdated ICE stream, while simplifying certificate handling and timer-based checks.

features.summary: RTCPeerConnection, the browser API used to set up WebRTC calls, received internal cleanup around object shutdown and frame-buffer handling. Firefox also avoids asking for WebRTC statistics again while an earlier request is still pending, reducing unnecessary work.

features.label: Negotiation engine (JSEP)

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Put at the session level if there is an RTP m-section.

features.summary: JSEP, the WebRTC session-negotiation process, now places a setting at the session level when the connection includes an RTP media section. A related build registration update helps ensure source headers are recognized; these are behind-the-scenes changes with no obvious interface change.

features.summary: Firefox updated its bundled libwebrtc build configuration for version 156 and included an Android lifecycle-lock component needed by that integration. This helps keep the browser's WebRTC engine building and working with its current upstream code.

features.summary: Firefox enabled a clang-tidy modernization check for SDP negotiation code. This is an internal code-quality improvement, with no visible change to how calls work.

features.summary: Firefox now rejects planar video images whose picture dimensions or layout are malformed. This prevents invalid image geometry from being passed into libwebrtc, the underlying WebRTC media engine.

features.summary: Firefox improved ICE, the process WebRTC uses to find a network path between callers, including fixes for connections that could stall and for removing old connection paths. It also adds DTLS restart support so encrypted connections can recover, improves compatibility with FIPS-compliant cryptography, and cleans up handling of mDNS-discovered candidates and media packets.

features.summary: WebRTC tests were made more reliable across operating systems, and several API behaviors were clarified: Firefox records the actual camera or microphone source granted, treats RTCSessionDescription fields as read-only, and cleans up correctly when screen sharing is rejected. The changes also adjust WebRTC DTLS key-share defaults and verify video features such as AV1 negotiation and the dependency descriptor RTP header extension, which helps receivers interpret video frames.

Firefox also reports capture-size changes only when they really happen and updates its DTLS security settings; other patches mainly improve codec capability checks and code quality.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Route MediaCapabilities WebRTC and encode paths through async codec support.

features.summary: Firefox strengthened how MediaCapabilities, the web API that lets sites ask which media formats a browser can handle, checks WebRTC audio and video encoding and decoding support. Those checks now follow a safer, asynchronous path, while video quality tracking and local RTP source reporting are kept in sync with libwebrtc; malformed image geometry is also rejected.

patches.subject: Merge directions when an RTP header extension is registered again with a different direction.

features.summary: WebRTC negotiation now rejects local session descriptions if their DTLS fingerprint—the value used to verify the encrypted connection—has been altered. It also improves AV1 format-parameter negotiation and keeps RTP header-extension directions consistent when extensions are registered more than once.

features.summary: Firefox fixed SDP parser handling of AV1 profile and level information, which helps WebRTC peers agree on compatible video formats. The remaining changes modernize internal code and update outdated references to the AV1 RTP specification.

features.label: libwebrtc build

features.summary: Firefox’s bundled libwebrtc build now includes Android’s `NativeLifecycleLock` Java component, which helps coordinate native code with Android’s lifecycle. The default build settings were also updated for libwebrtc versions 155 and 156, keeping Firefox’s build configuration in step with those releases.

features.label: Camera & audio capture

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Apply capture rotation centrally, behind a pref.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Don't swap the requested frame dimensions for rotated frames.

features.summary: Camera frame rotation is now applied in one central capture path, behind a preference, so different capture backends behave consistently. Requested width and height are preserved rather than being swapped just because the camera reports rotated frames.

features.label: Android camera capture

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Report rotation from the Android capture backend instead of applying it.

features.summary: On Android, the camera capture backend now reports the camera’s rotation directly instead of Firefox rotating the frames afterward. This keeps orientation information tied to the platform source and avoids duplicate or inconsistent rotation handling.

features.label: Libwebrtc Overrides

patches.author: Jens Stutte
patches.subject: Use std::source_location in WebrtcLocation.

features.summary: WebRTC’s diagnostic location information now uses C++ std::source_location, allowing source file and line details to be captured by the language rather than maintained through custom arguments. This is an internal reliability and maintainability improvement with no expected user-facing change.

features.label: Transportbridge

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Handle MediaTrackGraph promises on AbstractThread::MainThread().

features.summary: Media-track operations now handle their completion signals on the browser’s main thread, where they can be coordinated safely with other browser activity. This is an internal reliability change, with no intended visible change for users.

features.label: Video Engine

patches.author: Jan-Ivar Bruaroey
patches.subject: Store desktop capture sources in an nsTArray instead of a map.

features.summary: The video engine’s internal storage for desktop capture sources was changed. This is an implementation detail, with no user-visible behavior change indicated by the patch title.
